_README: HAND-EDITED. The pipeline reads this file and never writes it.
This is a pre-registration, not a watchlist. The thresholds are written
down BEFORE the evidence is looked at, because a tracker for a thesis
you already hold will otherwise find whatever you went looking for. If
a trigger never fires, that is a result. If you move a threshold after
seeing the data, write down that you moved it and why.
Three trigger types only: metric, price, event.
Every trigger must state a direction and a number. 'Capex slows' is not
a trigger. 'Combined trailing-four-quarter capex growth below 0% year
A trigger that cannot be evaluated reports STALE, which is not DORMANT.
DORMANT means we looked and the condition did not hold. STALE means we
could not look. They must never be rendered the same.

theses.title: The AI buildout is funded by four balance sheets
theses.statement: Hyperscaler capital expenditure is the demand under the AI complex. If the four largest spenders decelerate together, the revenue underneath the semiconductor and power trades goes with it, regardless of end-user demand for the models themselves.
theses.disconfirms: Capex keeps compounding while semiconductor revenue stalls anyway, which would mean the bottleneck is elsewhere and this thesis is watching the wrong variable.

triggers.what: Combined trailing-four-quarter capital expenditure, four hyperscalers
triggers.note: Point-in-time: a quarter counts from its FILED date, never its period end.
An early, weaker version of the one above. Expected to fire first and to be wrong more often.

theses.title: Inventory outgrowing revenue is what the top looks like in the accounts
theses.statement: In every prior semiconductor cycle, inventory kept building after demand turned, because orders were placed against a forecast that had already broken. The divergence shows up in the accounts a quarter or two before it shows up in guidance.
theses.disconfirms: Inventory builds and revenue keeps compounding anyway, which has happened during genuine supply constraint and would mean the build is deliberate rather than stranded.

triggers.what: Inventory growth minus revenue growth, year over year
triggers.note: Twenty points is the threshold because smaller gaps are ordinary seasonality.

triggers.what: Days sales outstanding, year over year change
triggers.note: What vendor financing looks like from outside: revenue recognised, cash not collected.

theses.title: The people with the most information are selling
theses.statement: Officers and directors at the AI complex sell for many reasons and most of them are uninformative. A sharp CLUSTER of large sales across several issuers in a short window is a different object from steady scheduled selling.
theses.disconfirms: A cluster fires and the complex keeps rising, which is the base rate and the reason this trigger is weak on its own.

triggers.what: Distinct issuers in the AI complex with officer or director sales above the value floor, in a rolling window
triggers.note: UNIVERSE NAMED EXPLICITLY. 'The AI complex' is not a set a tracker can evaluate; these fifteen tickers are. GOOGL is absent from our Form 4 data entirely. NOT YET EVALUABLE: 18,647 of 18,701 insider_sales rows are dated 2026-06-01 or later, so these names carry about four months of history, not four years. Every candidate threshold calibrated to the same figure -- one episode, ~3.1/yr -- which is an artifact of one continuous window rather than a base rate. Until the history is backfilled this reports STALE. A threshold chosen now would be a number with nothing behind it.

theses.title: The buildout is partly debt-funded and rates are the constraint
theses.statement: Datacenter construction and GPU purchases are increasingly financed rather than paid from cash flow. A widening in credit stress raises the hurdle rate on the marginal datacenter before it shows up in any company's accounts.
theses.disconfirms: Credit widens sharply and capex continues, meaning the spending is cash-funded and insensitive to financing cost.

triggers.what: High-yield versus long Treasury, as a ratio
triggers.source: Polygon daily closes, HYG and TLT
triggers.note: A proxy, not a spread. Real option-adjusted spreads are not available on free data and this must not be described as one. The pair is named explicitly rather than left to a default in code, for the same reason the insider trigger lists its fifteen tickers: a universe the tracker infers is one nobody can check. No threshold was changed when this was added.

triggers.what: Ten-year minus two-year Treasury par yield
triggers.source: Treasury daily yield curve, already collected as a gauge

theses.title: Price confirms, late and without explanation
theses.statement: Price is the weakest evidence here and the only one that is never ABSENT. It is included so the record shows what the complex was doing while every other trigger sat dormant.
theses.disconfirms: Nothing. This is a thermometer, not a thesis, and it is labelled as one.

_not_measurable._note: Named explicitly so their absence is a stated limit of this tracker rather than a silent gap. A trigger that cannot be evaluated must not exist here pretending to be DORMANT.
_not_measurable.datacenter_power_and_permits: No free structured source. Utility interconnection queues are published inconsistently and per-region.
_not_measurable.private_ai_company_finances: OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI and similar do not file. The largest demand signals in this thesis are invisible to EDGAR by construction.
_not_measurable.export_controls: Policy events have no structured feed and arrive as prose.
_not_measurable.inference_cost_curves: Not disclosed by anyone in a comparable form.
_not_measurable.circular_and_vendor_financing_deals: Visible only in filing prose. Lane D Phase 0 measured free-text extraction from 8-K exhibits at 21 HIT, 2 MISSED, 37 ABSENT over 60 releases, so a trigger built on it would report ABSENT most of the time and could not be trusted when it did not.
_not_measurable.depreciation_useful_life_changes: Stated in accounting-policy prose rather than a comparable XBRL tag. Same extraction problem as above.

_data_defects._note: Found while calibrating. Recorded because a tracker that reads these tables should know what is wrong with them.
_data_defects.insider_sales_bad_prices: Seven sales priced above $2,000/share, six of them IHT between $22,593 and $52,316 on a single-digit stock. Only two carry the suspect flag, so the flag under-catches.
_data_defects.insider_sales_duplicates: FANG 2026-09-16 appears twice with identical shares and price. Co-filer double-counting, already on the backlog as W2.
_data_defects.insider_sales_depth: 18,647 of 18,701 rows are dated 2026-06-01 or later. Anything calibrated against this table is calibrated against four months.
